text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (E 200 estate) states the cabin is quiet and the car is well suited to long motorway trips. Owner praises the driver assistance: adaptive cruise, semi-autonomous steering for 20-30 seconds, automatic braking and camera/radar aids that help in fog. Owner likes the navigation based on Google Maps. Owner reports fuel use of about 7.0-7.1 l/100 km on a mixed route with the E 200 petrol estate.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (E 400 e plug-in hybrid saloon) states the engine is noticeably noisy and buzzy at low revs, louder than comparable BMW or Audi diesels, and recommends driving electrically where possible. Owner reports a creaking/scraping noise when lifting off the throttle, also at idle; the dealer suspects the turbo wastegate valve but the owner is not convinced.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (E 220 d saloon, under 1.90 m) states the front headrests cannot be raised or moved back and press on the neck, causing neck and shoulder pain on long drives; the dealer only offers a modification that would void the warranty, and the owner rates the W213 far better.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (review text describes the E 300 de diesel plug-in hybrid) states that under firm acceleration in electric mode the drive briefly disconnects before the combustion engine and then the e-motor join in.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (E 220 d saloon) reports about 5.9 l/100 km on average and over 1,400 km on one tank at up to 140 km/h. Owner states the car is very quiet. Owner reports no faults after about six months and over 30,000 km.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (E 220 d saloon) reports the flush door handles did not extend, so the car could not be opened with the key fob or phone and a spare key was needed. Owner reports a gearbox fault warning before a service visit, which had cleared by the time the technician arrived.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (E 220 d saloon) describes the car as very comfortable. Owner reports economical running at about 5 l/100 km at 130 km/h on the motorway. Owner states the voice assistant talks too much and interrupts.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (E 200 petrol saloon) reports 14 visits to the service centre, without further detail.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (EQE 350 saloon) states the ride is very comfortable and absorbs bumps well. Owner rates the EQE's quietness above their previous Peugeot 508s and Kia Sorento. Owner praises the standard audio system as better than in their previous cars. Owner reports over 500 km of range in summer with average consumption of about 18 kWh/100 km.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (EQE 300 saloon) states comfort is far better than in their previous Tesla Model 3 Long Range. Owner, initially worried about rear-wheel drive, reports that on snow and ice in the mountains the stability systems quickly brought the car back in line when they deliberately provoked a slide, unlike their previous Tesla.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (EQE 350 saloon) states the motor has enough power for daily driving in all conditions.
